Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

paneffectR 0.1.2

Heatmap styles

  • plot_heatmap() gains a style argument with three ready-made looks: "clean" (new default: one hue on a light grey grid), "pan" (rows split into Core / Accessory / Unique blocks with a coloured side bar; binary cells take the class colour) and "mono" (black on white for print).
  • All styles label the legend “Absent”/“Present” with a meaningful title, draw a light grid between cells on matrices of up to 200 rows, use slimmer dendrograms and angled column labels. Score matrices use an orange ramp so they are not mistaken for presence/absence; count matrices whose maximum is 1 use the binary colours.
  • Arguments passed through ... to ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap() now override the style’s settings instead of erroring on duplicate arguments.
  • New vignette, “Styling Heatmaps”, covering the three styles, shared arguments, saving figures and how to go further with ComplexHeatmap. README and the other vignettes use the new styles.

paneffectR 0.1.1

Fixes from a new-user functional test pass (see GitHub issues for details).

Bug fixes

  • FASTA headers with descriptions (e.g. NCBI, UniProt, BRAKER output) no longer silently break clustering. load_fasta() now uses the first whitespace-delimited token as protein_id and keeps the remainder in a new description column. cluster_proteins() also validates that DIAMOND’s IDs map back to loaded proteins.
  • Nucleotide FASTA input (which made DIAMOND hang indefinitely) is detected and rejected with a clear error, both at load time and before clustering. External tool calls now have a timeout (default 3600 s).
  • build_pa_matrix(score_threshold = ) no longer crashes when some assemblies have no score file; orthogroups without any score are dropped rather than erroring.
  • tool_path and conda_prefix containing ~ are expanded before use.
  • cluster_proteins() gains conda_env to use a named conda/mamba environment, matching the documented resolution order.
  • Gzipped FASTA files (*.faa.gz) now yield the correct assembly name so score files are found.
  • Trailing stop codons (*) are stripped and sequences upper-cased on load.
  • plot_upset() no longer emits ggplot2 deprecation warnings from UpSetR.

Improvements

  • load_proteins() prints a one-line summary and warns about missing score files, score IDs that match no FASTA IDs, empty FASTA files and single-assembly input.
  • load_scores() errors clearly when protein_id or custom_score is missing.
  • cluster_proteins() reports progress for each step and the temporary directory when keep_temp = TRUE. Use quiet = TRUE to silence.
  • plot_heatmap() is much faster: Jaccard and Bray-Curtis distances are vectorised, and matrices with more than max_cluster_rows rows (default 5000) are ordered by clustering distinct presence/absence patterns.
  • print() for protein_collection reports whether scores are loaded.

Documentation

  • README install instructions use pak/remotes (devtools >= 2.5 no longer bundles install_github()), and build_pa_matrix() examples pass proteins.
  • ?load_proteins documents file naming conventions and the score CSV format.
  • All exported functions now have runnable examples.
  • Fixed non-running vignette code (row.names typo; hard-coded assembly name).

Breaking changes

  • filter_by_score() (an unimplemented stub) has been removed. Use build_pa_matrix(score_threshold = ).
  • cluster_proteins(method = ) only accepts "diamond_rbh"; the unimplemented "orthofinder" and "mmseqs2" values are no longer listed.
  • load_fasta() returns an additional description column.

paneffectR 0.1.0

Initial release of paneffectR. ## Features

Data Loading

  • load_proteins() loads multiple FASTA files with optional effector scores
  • load_fasta(), load_scores(), load_name_mapping() for individual files
  • Support for omnieff pipeline output format

Clustering

  • cluster_proteins() with DIAMOND RBH + expansion algorithm
  • Configurable identity, coverage, and e-value thresholds

Matrix Building

  • build_pa_matrix() creates presence/absence matrices from clustering results
  • Binary, count, and score-based matrix types
  • Score threshold filtering for effector analysis
  • Optional singleton inclusion

Visualization

  • plot_heatmap() with ComplexHeatmap backend
    • Row and column clustering
    • Multiple distance metrics (binary, Jaccard, Bray-Curtis)
    • Row and column annotations
  • plot_upset() for set intersection visualization
  • plot_scores() for effector score distributions
  • plot_dendro() for assembly clustering dendrograms

Utilities

  • get_singletons(), n_singletons(), singletons_by_assembly() for singleton analysis
  • check_tool_installed(), find_tool() for external tool management

Documentation

  • Getting Started vignette with core workflow
  • Effector Analysis vignette for omnieff users
  • Pan-Genome Analysis vignette for general comparisons
  • Algorithm Deep Dive vignette with technical details
